details: The Federal Reserve unanimously kept the federal funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% during its June meeting but revised its expected end-2026 rate projection to 3.8% and PCE inflation forecast to 3.6%. May's Consumer Price Index (CPI) had reached 4.2%, the highest in three years, underscoring persistent inflation concerns. Comments from former Fed Governor Randy Kroszner highlighted a growing trust deficit regarding inflation, suggesting interest rates may remain elevated for an extended period. This hawkish stance could dampen risk appetite for cryptocurrencies. The market is now closely watching the upcoming June CPI data on July 14th for further cues.
title: Fed Maintains Rates, Signals 'Higher for Longer' Amid Stubborn Inflation

details: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have escalated following Iran's declaration that it would not resume negotiations with the United States until Washington alters its "pressure-driven policies." This diplomatic impasse, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz, has heightened market risk premiums and contributed to rising oil prices. The increased uncertainty is prompting investors to seek safe-haven assets, potentially reducing demand for riskier assets such as cryptocurrencies.
title: Mideast Tensions Rise as Iran Rejects US Talks, Impacting Oil and Risk Markets

details: The cryptocurrency market is anticipating significant volatility ahead of the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data release for June, scheduled for July 14th. This crucial inflation report will heavily influence the Federal Reserve's future monetary policy decisions. Adding to market caution, a substantial $1.4 billion in Bitcoin options expired on July 10th, contributing to short-term price movements. While spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen some tentative inflows, the overall sentiment remains mixed.
title: US CPI Release & Bitcoin Options Expiry Set to Drive Crypto Volatility
